title: Chart rendering improvements
description: Improve sparkline and yearly chart visual quality based on design review of graph-lab output. Six targeted fixes across both chart types.

title: Fix yearly X-axis month/date label collision
description:
CRITICAL. In yearly_generator.go, month name labels (drawYearlyMonthMarkers, y+height+15) collide with rotated biweekly date labels (drawYearlyBiweeklyTicks, y+height+25). The two label systems render on top of each other.

Fix: Remove the biweekly date text labels entirely. Keep only the short biweekly tick marks (the vertical lines at the bottom of the chart). Month names at y+height+15 become the sole text labels on the X-axis. Weekly ticks remain as-is (no text). Start/end date labels at y+height+50 remain.

Affected functions:
- drawYearlyBiweeklyTicks (line ~556): remove the DrawStringAnchored call and the Push/Translate/Rotate block, keep the tick line drawing
- drawYearlyMonthMarkers (line ~501): no change needed
- drawYearlyWeeklyTicks (line ~645): no change needed
- drawYearlyStartEndLabels (line ~710): no change needed

Validate: Run make graph-lab-yearly and visually confirm no label overlap in all 5 yearly scenarios.

title: Round Y-axis to nice numbers (both charts)
description:
Both sparkline and yearly charts show raw calculated Y-axis bounds (e.g. -8.1%, 24.2%) instead of clean rounded values (-10%, 25%).

Fix: Implement a niceNumber() utility function that rounds axis bounds outward to visually clean intervals. Algorithm (Heckbert's nice numbers):
1. Given data min/max, calculate the range
2. Pick a 'nice' tick spacing from {1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50} scaled to the range magnitude
3. Round min down and max up to the nearest tick multiple
4. Update labels to show the rounded values

Apply to:
- generator.go calculateYRange(): round finalMin down, finalMax up to nice intervals before returning
- yearly_generator.go calculateYearlyYRange(): same treatment
- drawLabels / drawYearlyLabels: display the rounded values instead of raw floats

Create a shared helper in a new file internal/sparkline/axis.go (or add to generator.go) with niceNumber(value float64, round bool) float64 and niceRange(min, max float64) (niceMin, niceMax float64).

Validate: Run make graph-lab, confirm all 10 charts show round Y-axis numbers (e.g. -10%, 0%, 10%, 25%, not -8.1%, 24.2%).

title: Add intermediate X-axis time labels to 48-hour sparkline
description:
The 48-hour sparkline only shows start and end times on the X-axis. No intermediate labels, making it impossible to locate mid-chart events.

Fix: The existing drawDayMarkers function already draws midnight UTC vertical lines with day labels for multi-day data. Enhance it to also add 6-hour or 12-hour intermediate tick marks with time labels.

In generator.go drawLabels():
- The multi-day branch (timeRange >= 1 day) already calls drawDayMarkers. Add additional hour markers at 06:00, 12:00, 18:00 UTC with smaller font/lighter color.
- The same-day branch shows only start/end labels. Add midpoint label.

Keep the midnight day labels (Mon, Tue etc.) as the primary markers. The hour labels should be secondary (smaller font, lighter color, shorter tick lines).

Validate: Run make graph-lab-sparkline, confirm all 5 sparkline scenarios have readable intermediate time references.

title: Reduce yearly X-axis tick density
description:
After fixing the label collision (gjw.1), the yearly charts still have too many vertical tick marks at the bottom. The combination of monthly + biweekly + weekly ticks creates visual noise.

Fix: Remove the weekly ticks entirely (drawYearlyWeeklyTicks). Keep only monthly grid lines (full height) and biweekly tick marks (short lines, no text per gjw.1). This gives a cleaner bottom edge.

In yearly_generator.go:
- Remove the call to drawYearlyWeeklyTicks from drawYearlyLabels (line ~468)
- Optionally remove the drawYearlyWeeklyTicks and findYearlyWeeklyPositions functions, or keep them for future use

Validate: Run make graph-lab-yearly, confirm the bottom edge of all 5 yearly charts looks cleaner with fewer tick marks.

title: Boost zone watermark contrast (both charts)
description:
The 'Positive', 'Neutral', 'Negative' background text watermarks are nearly invisible in all charts due to extremely low alpha values.

Current values:
- Neutral zone: color.RGBA{200, 200, 200, 30} (alpha 30/255 = 12% opacity)
- Positive: color.RGBA{40, 167, 69, 60} (alpha 60/255 = 24% opacity)
- Negative: color.RGBA{220, 53, 69, 60} (alpha 60/255 = 24% opacity)

Fix: Increase alpha values to make the text readable but still clearly 'background':
- Neutral: alpha 30 -> 60
- Positive: alpha 60 -> 100
- Negative: alpha 60 -> 100

Apply to both files:
- generator.go drawNeutralWatermark (line ~265), drawSentimentWatermarks (lines ~301, ~316)
- yearly_generator.go drawYearlyNeutralWatermark (line ~261), drawYearlySentimentWatermarks (lines ~289, ~302)

Validate: Run make graph-lab, confirm zone labels are legible but not distracting in all 10 charts.

title: Improve yearly trend line contrast over green data
description:
The blue dashed Gaussian trend line (color.RGBA{0, 123, 255, 255}) loses visibility when overlapping green positive data segments (color.RGBA{40, 167, 69, 255}). Blue-on-green has poor contrast.

Fix options (pick one):
A) Draw a white 'halo' behind the trend line: render the trend line twice — first pass with white color and thicker width (e.g. 3.5px), second pass with blue at 1.5px. This creates an outline effect.
B) Change the trend line color to something that contrasts with both green and red, such as dark purple (color.RGBA{100, 50, 150, 255}) or dark teal.
C) Use a solid (non-dashed) line with lower opacity for the trend.

Option A (white halo) is recommended as it preserves the current blue color identity while ensuring visibility over any data color.

Apply to:
- yearly_generator.go drawYearlyGaussianTrendLine (line ~896)
- generator.go drawGaussianTrendLine (line ~733) — apply same treatment for consistency

Validate: Run make graph-lab, confirm trend line is visible in yearly-steadily-positive (all green data) and yearly-seasonal (mixed colors).
